newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi blasts Washington's human rights record.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi blasts Washington's human rights record.

text.p: Vietnam on Wednesday dismissed a U.S. State Department report on human rights and accused Washington of hundreds of years of abuses.

A lengthy commentary in the Communist Party's Nhan Dan newspaper said the State Department's annual report, issued last week, was using human rights as an outdated pretext for interference in the internal affairs of Asian nations.

"In fact, the United States is the country that has violated most seriously human rights at home and abroad ... since Independence the United States has conducted about 70 wars both at home and abroad, depriving the right to life from a lot of people in other countries, including the Vietnam War," it said.
The commentary highlighted racial problems and described the United States as one of the world's most violent societies.
The State Department report criticised scores of countries including Vietnam.
"The Government's (Hanoi's) human rights record continued to be poor," it said. "The Government continued to repress basic political and some religious freedoms and to commit numerous abuses."

It referred to reports that some prisons used forced labour for commercial ventures, quoted estimates that Vietnam was holding between 70 and 1,000 political prisoners, and criticised the behaviour of members of the powerful internal security agency.
Vietnam has reacted with anger on several occasions to criticism of its human rights record from overseas.
Party officials say rights issues are being used by forces intent on undermining confidence in Vietnam's socialist system.
